1_I_DID_NOT_BUILD_THE_THREE_CASCADES_AND.what: `RI-VIS04` §3's MIN BAR is `3 cascades × 2048², PCF 3×3 minimum, shadow distance ≥ 150 m`. My brief named this and the retention hard fail together as 'the work'. I closed the retention hard fail and I did NOT build the cascades.
1_I_DID_NOT_BUILD_THE_THREE_CASCADES_AND.what_I_did_instead: VERIFIED the MIN BAR live rather than leaving it UNVERIFIED for a fourth round, and corrected my own instrument when it got the count wrong. Read off the running scene at four orbit angles at 08:00: shadow-casting directional lights whose PARENT CHAIN IS VISIBLE = **1**, `mapSize` **4096**, fitted extent **285.691 m**, texel **0.06975 m**, `shadow.camera.far` **725.691**, `shadowMap.type` **PCFSoftShadowMap**, `shadowDistance` **150**, `moon.castShadow` **false**.

clause_by_clause.2048² per cascade: N/A while there is one map; that map is 4096².
clause_by_clause.PCF 3×3 minimum: MET — `PCFSoftShadowMap`, read live and confirmed at `game/src/render/renderer.js:89`.

1_I_DID_NOT_BUILD_THE_THREE_CASCADES_AND.why_I_stopped: three.js has no cascaded shadow map, so real CSM here means N co-directional lights plus a global override of the `lights_fragment_begin` shader chunk to mask every cascade but the fragment's own — a seam into EVERY material in the game, on a shared tree, with three other agents driving browsers off it. `HAZARDS.md` §26 records that one backtick in a shader template literal killed every browser tool on the branch. I judged that shipping an unverified whole-scene shader patch was worse than shipping a verified hard-fail fix plus an honest 'not built'. That judgement is mine and a critic should feel free to overturn it.
1_I_DID_NOT_BUILD_THE_THREE_CASCADES_AND.what_the_next_round_inherits_rather_than: The design is worked out and the blockers are named: (a) three.js sorts shadow-casting lights first (`shadowCastingAndTexturingLightsFirst`), so cascade lights added first at scene root occupy directional indices 0..N-1 deterministically and `UNROLLED_LOOP_INDEX` can select them; (b) the split distances must be GLSL CONSTANTS baked at install time, because `cloneUniforms` copies values and a shared per-frame uniform does not reach materials already compiled; (c) weights `w0 = 1-smoothstep(s0±b)`, `w1 = smoothstep(s0±b)*(1-smoothstep(s1±b))`, `w2 = smoothstep(s1±b)` sum to exactly 1, which is what stops N lights being N× the light — the failure `sky.js:701` predicts as 'a step in the shadow STRENGTH at each split'; (d) a fragment outside a fitted box returns 1.0 (lit) from three's own frustum test, so `R.shadow`'s per-recipe distance multiplier can keep scaling the FIT while the splits stay constant. Texel density at splits [20 m, 60 m, 150 m] would go 0.0698 → about 0.0117 m in the near cascade, a 6× improvement in exactly the band the player looks at.
1_I_DID_NOT_BUILD_THE_THREE_CASCADES_AND.cost_of_not_doing_it: §3 is scored against an unmet MIN BAR. It is not a hard fail and it did not cap this item; the retention clause did.

The FIRST reading of the session was **WAIT** — 4 browser instances, load 16.12 over 4 cores = 4.03 per core, at or over the ceiling — and I did not launch on it. three-gpu-pathtracer.and_this_time_upstream_WAS_opened: My brief recorded that round 3's disposition was honest but 'opened no upstream source'. I fetched four files from the pinned commit `3c6cda19d1788d7d93705eee704328e66823c845` this turn: `README.md` (17,560 B), `LICENSE` (1,072 B), `package.json` (2,103 B) and `src/core/WebGLPathTracer.js` (12,098 B). `src/core/PhysicalPathTracingMaterial.js` returned 404 at that path and the GitHub contents API is not enabled for this session, so I could not enumerate `src/` — a limit, stated.
three-gpu-pathtracer.registry_claims_verified_against_upstrea: `package.json` at the pin reads `version 0.0.24`, `license MIT`, peers `three >=0.180.0`, `three-mesh-bvh >=0.7.4`, `xatlas-web ^0.1.0` — the registry's pin, licence and peer list are correct verbatim. `LICENSE` is MIT, Copyright (c) 2021 Garrett Johnson. The registry's boundary quote 'instanced geometry as unsupported' is upstream's README line 581 verbatim.
three-gpu-pathtracer.THE_DECISIVE_REASON_AND_IT_IS_ONE_THE_RE: Upstream's own Gotchas list says **'Only MeshStandardMaterial and MeshPhysicalMaterial are supported.'** F4's subject is the sky and the air. This build's sky is a `THREE.ShaderMaterial` (`sky.js` `SKY_VERT`/`SKY_FRAG` on a BackSide sphere), its precipitation is a `LineBasicMaterial`, and its atmosphere is a custom `HeightFog`. A path-traced frame of this scene would therefore be a frame **with no sky and no atmosphere in it** — it would omit precisely the thing the item exists to judge. That is a stronger and more specific decline than 'M6 runs on our raster pixels', and it comes from opened source rather than from our own file.
three-gpu-pathtracer.two_further_upstream_facts_worth_recordi: (1) `WebGLPathTracer.js:12` gates on `renderer.extensions.get('EXT_float_blend')`, and every capture in this item is SwiftShader — whether the oracle would run at all on this box is untested. (2) `WebGLPathTracer.js:108` constructs `PathTracingRenderer(renderer)` on the SAME `WebGLRenderer` and line 143 calls `this._renderer.render(scene, camera)`, so it takes the shipped renderer over rather than sitting beside it.
three-gpu-pathtracer.recommended_registry_correction: The candidate's **Boundary** line names instancing and `setScene` cost but NOT the material restriction, which is the clause that actually decides F4. Adding it would save the next mapped builder the fetch.
three-gpu-pathtracer.rule_4: `IMPLEMENTATION-LEADS.md` rule 4: 'a `declined` finding completes the evaluation. It creates no follow-on work by itself.'

how_the_lever_was_chosen_and_the_prior_i.step_2_the_ablation_said_IT_IS_NOT: Ten page-side arms at pair03 across two processes. The two controls are **bit-identical between separate processes** — `retention` 0.2324, `C_shadow_med` 0.005964, `C_local_med` 0.025657 to six decimal places — so this run's own floor on every M6 number is **0.0000**.
how_the_lever_was_chosen_and_the_prior_i.THE_RESULT: `env2` and `hemi4-fill4` reach the SAME shadow brightness — 0.0721 against 0.0755, a 5% difference — and land on OPPOSITE SIDES OF THE HARD FAIL, 0.2737 against 0.4141. **`retention` is not a function of how bright the shadow is.** Read as retention gained per unit of shadow luminance gained, the two lamp terms buy **5.25, 5.34 and 5.25** (arms a2, a10, a11) and the probe buys **1.32** — the lamps are about 4× more efficient than the probe.
how_the_lever_was_chosen_and_the_prior_i.AND_MY_SECOND_PRIOR_WAS_ALSO_FALSIFIED: I expected the HemisphereLight to beat the flat AmbientLight, because a hemisphere's contribution depends on the surface normal and a flat ambient's does not, so the hemisphere ought to add structure rather than a constant. Arms a9 (hemi only) and a10 (fill only) are indistinguishable per unit of shadow luminance — 4.84 and 5.34. **Normal-dependence is NOT the mechanism.** I have ablated WHICH term moves the number and I have NOT ablated WHY, and per S63 I am not going to narrate one; both the numerator and the denominator are published above so the next reader can take it further.
how_the_lever_was_chosen_and_the_prior_i.why_x4_and_not_x8: x8 reaches `retention` 0.5469 — still short of the 0.60 profile minimum, which is a SOFT fail — for +44% mean frame luminance. x4 clears the HARD fail with 38% margin, clears `C_shadow` outright, and costs +20% (`mean_Yp_fg` 0.1554 → 0.1863). Buying a soft fail with a 44% exposure lift is S59's trade and I refused it.

What it is NOT is evidence that the morning is fine.

JOB_2 — SECTION 2-D3, APPLIED AS A GATE,.WHERE_2_D3_COSTS_ME_AND_I_AM_NOT_HIDING_: At **pair01's full frame** `hue_offset` fell **6.37 → 4.80** across my change. What I cannot say is that the frame got better there.

the_59_1_percent_figure_re_derived_and_i.how: Parsed the `WEATHER` table out of `game/src/render/sky.js` and applied `recipeForConditions()`'s own thresholds (`storm` if `rain >= 0.8 || overcast >= 0.94`; `overcast-flat` if `overcast >= 0.50`), this turn, in one command.
the_59_1_percent_figure_re_derived_and_i.result: **43** weather states are declared, not 20. **7** route to `storm` (storm, heavy_rain, sea_squall, downpour, gale, hail, ash_storm) and **23** route to `overcast-flat`. **30 of 43 = 69.8%**, not 59.1%.
the_59_1_percent_figure_re_derived_and_i.the_honest_caveat_which_the_inherited_fi: That is a fraction of DECLARED STATES, not of daylight TIME. States are not equiprobable and I did not measure the transition table, so a time-weighted figure is unmeasured. Both the old number and mine are state counts wearing a time claim, and neither should be quoted as 'x% of daylight' without the weather-transition data.
